newsitem.title: FRANCE: French author dies after dictating book by winks.
newsitem.headline: French author dies after dictating book by winks.

text.p: A French journalist, paralysed and made mute by illness and who dictated a 150-page book letter after letter by winking his left eye, has died less than a week after its publication, friends said on Monday.
Jean-Dominique Bauby, former editor-in-chief of the women's weekly Elle, died in hospital near Paris. He was 45.
Bauby had been lying motionless since suffering a stroke 15 months ago which left him paralysed except for his left eye but with his intellect untouched.

Publishers Robert Laffont last week released the book "Le Scaphandre et le Papillon" (The Diving Suit and the Butterfly) which Bauby "dictated" to a copywriter by winking when the correct letter of the alphabet was pronounced.
Copywriter Claude Mendibil said she spent six hours daily with Bauby taking down the text he had endlessly repeated in his head.
As their communication code improved, Bauby went from dictating half a page a day to almost three pages a day.
Bauby winked once for 'yes' and twice for 'no'. Mendibil read out the letters in the order of those most frequently used in the French language.
